summary: No authorization bypass was found in the reviewed Firestore rules and authenticated sync boundary after the fixes below. The score reflects the specified checklist and emulator coverage, not a guarantee of exhaustive security or a deployed-backend verification. Legacy direct writes remain available until the deliberate server-side protocol cutoff; device timestamps remain untrusted audit claims.

findings.issue: A legacy cached private note with no revision could reject its first revisioned server update locally and retain stale text after acknowledgement.
findings.recommendation: Normalize missing legacy revisions to zero; retain the new regression test alongside financial reconciliation tests.

findings.issue: New local commands lacked an explicit binding between their capture actor and the authenticated account used for upload during an account-switch race.
findings.recommendation: Require the local namespace to match the authenticated user before enqueue/upload and reject mismatched claimed actor IDs server-side. The claimed actor is a binding check, never a source of authority. Preserve support for previously captured v1 commands without that optional field.

findings.issue: The sync void validator checked session expiry without explicitly rejecting a session whose operational start was still in the future; session creation also allowed a short future-start grace window.
findings.recommendation: Reject future session starts and require startsAt <= server time < endsAt for voids. Keep the future-session regression test.
